newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - T-bond correction seen postponed again.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - T-bond correction seen postponed again.

text.p: A long-anticipated correction in U.S. Treasury bond futures appeared to be postponed again after this morning's strong bounce, despite concerns over overstretched oscillator charts, technical analysts said.

June T-bonds bounced to the mid-110 area by mid-morning, up more than half a point on the day, after dipping early to 109-22/32, below Tuesday's lows. An unexpected drop in April producer price index soothed fears of an interest rate hike at the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
"That negates Tuesday's key reversal down," said Ken Seehusen, editor of analytical newsletter Chart Insight.
June bonds had an "outside day" on Tuesday after touching a 2-1/2 month high of 110-22/32 early in the day and then skidding below Monday's bottom to a low of 109-24/32.
Seehusen said another outside day today with a close above Tuesday's high would open the door for a rally toward 112-10/32.
That projection, based on his proprietary model, coincided with a 75-percent retracement of the February-April decline and with the reaction highs on February 25 and 26, he noted.
Seehusen added that he was not concerned about the oversold conditions in short-term momentum indicators.
"The market in my opinion has entered a trending move to the upside, and a lot of times your biggest moves come when the market is in an overbought condition," he said.

"You've had a fresh shot in the arm from some fresh fundamental news," he added, referring to this morning's prices data. PPI fell by 0.6 percent overall in April, against average forecasts that it would be unchanged and March's 0.1 percent drop.
Still, Jim Bohan, senior futures strategist at Merrill Lynch Capital Markets, saw little room for further gains in T-bonds.
He said the PPI, even though it was good news, was like "looking into the rear-view mirror" and that if the Fed did not raise rates it could even be a negative factor for bonds.
"What I'm looking at now is a loss of momentum on this recovery trend we've been in in the last couple of weeks," Bohan said. "I really don't think we're going to be able to go a great deal further."
He said the dollar's sharp decline in the past week, strength in gold prices and a breakout higher in the Commodity Research Bureau index were also likely to eventually take their toll.
The CRB index, which last week pierced above resistance consisting of various old highs in the 248-249 area, was off 0.40 point at 250.90 in mid-morning.
Bohan expected June T-bonds to test the 108-1/2 to 109 area fairly soon and then the 106 to 107 area, toward the 106-12/32 April lows, in the coming month or so.
